To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the MPM model describes better than the UPM model the evolutionary process of genes and that there are two pacemakers in the genome of bacteria.
the MPM model is more accurate than the UPM and that the number of genomic universal pacemakers is two.
the universal molecular pacemaker model is not universal and there are two pacemakers.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the problem of identifying genomic pacemakers and the number of them.
a geometric approach to identify the number of genomic clocks, and to identify the genes that are affected by each clock.
the problem of finding a set of genes that share a common pacemaker.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
there are at least two pacemakers and possibly more.
the MPM model, with two pacemakers, is superior to the UPM with a single pacemaker and to the MC model, and that it describes the evolutionary process more precisely.
the MPM model describes the data better than the UPM model.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the MPM model is more general than UPM, but it is more difficult to estimate.
the UPM and MPM models are better than the MC in explaining the evolutionary process and that the MPM model provides better fit to data than UPM.
the UPM is not the only model capable of explaining the evolutionary process.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the MPM model can be applied to a variety of biological problems where the genes are affected by multiple pacemakers, such as in gene regulation, gene expression and protein-protein interaction networks.
the number of pacemaker is not confined to a single number, rather it can vary across taxa and even across genes.
the UPM is not a single model, but rather a family of models, where the number of pacemaker is a free parameter that can be inferred.
